entries.title: Federal Court Says States Can Regulate Prediction Market Sites
entries.summary: The ruling is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court.
entries.content:
States can regulate prediction market platforms as a form of gambling, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled Friday, opening the door for state-by-state regulation of companies like Kalshi.

The ruling from a three-judge panel of Trump appointees upends the status quo for prediction market sites that had, up until this week, been only subject to federal regulations.

“The substance of the sports event contracts offered on Kalshi's DCM is sports gambling, regardless of whether Kalshi calls them swaps,” the ruling reads. “Just as ‘that which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet,’ ... placing sports bets, even when called by another name, is still gambling.”

Prediction markets like Kalshi allow users to place wagers on the outcome of a wide array of events, and have long maintained they are legally distinct from gambling and are solely subject to regulation by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The company is expected to appeal the ruling.

Under the Trump administration, the CFTC sued a handful of states seeking to regulate prediction markets, actively supporting Kalshi as it faced lawsuits from states’ attorneys general.

Friday’s ruling came after regulators in Nevada sued to challenge the CFTC’s view that only it could regulate the companies.

“If prediction markets are allowed everywhere, and then they basically just become quick access to sports gambling, like there's your loophole, there’s the back door,” Rep. Blake Moore, a Republican from Utah, where gambling is banned, told NOTUS in an interview before the ruling. “I could not be more of a die-hard supporter of my governor and my attorney general for keeping this at bay and making sure that the legal elements take place to allow Utah to control its own destiny.”

Kalshi did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

entries.title: ICE Detains Far-Right Commentator Milo Yiannopoulos
entries.summary: The British national has been an outspoken supporter of mass deportations.
entries.content:
Milo Yiannopoulos, the far-right provocateur who has been feuding with MAGAworld, is in immigration detention after being apprehended outside of New Orleans.

Immigration agents detained the former Kanye West spokesperson and Marjorie Taylor Greene congressional intern Thursday at the airport, the Department of Homeland Security said in a statement Friday. A judge ordered Yiannopoulos to be removed on July 22 after he failed to appear in immigration court, according to the agency.

Yiannopoulos is from the United Kingdom and has been an outspoken supporter of mass deportations and Immigration and Customs Enforcement crackdowns.

“If ICE has 90,000 employees, and all we are asking for is 10,000 deportations a day, that’s 9 agents per illegal. More than enough to cover investigation, apprehension and removal,” Yiannopoulos posted on X in the early days of President Donald Trump’s second term. “What are they all waiting for?”

Yiannopoulos entered the country legally in 2019 but “chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws,” a DHS spokesperson said.

Trump confidant Laura Loomer took credit for Yiannopoulos’ detention, saying she exposed his status as an “illegal alien.” She also called for Greene to face an investigation for hiring Yiannopoulos in the past, saying she has “a whole hard drive full of receipts” to give to the Justice Department about their “sinister relationship.”

“Milo is going back to where he came from: HELL,” Loomer wrote on X.

entries.title: Trump Plans to Freeze Civilian Federal Worker Pay for Next Year
entries.summary: The president made a similar move last year but ultimately reversed course.
entries.content:
Most civilian federal employees would not receive a pay raise next year in an alternative compensation plan released by President Donald Trump this week.

“Such a large raise for Federal employees while most Americans still struggle with the consequences of the Biden Administration’s giant inflation spree is unacceptable and would be unfair,” Trump wrote in a letter to Congress this week, first reported by Federal News Network.

“I have therefore decided to set at zero the pay adjustment to be made for the 2027 pay year.”

Federal law enforcement and military personnel would be exempted, with active officers across those categories receiving anywhere from a 3.6% to 7% pay raise, the letter says.

“I strongly support the members of our Armed Forces, who are the greatest fighting force in the world and the defenders of American freedom,” Trump wrote. “We must work to rebuild our military’s readiness and capabilities by supporting our service members and their families.”

The Trump administration’s proposal to freeze salaries comes as the president has cracked down on job protections and expansion opportunities for federal employees. The White House forecast these moves in its April budget request for the upcoming fiscal year.

Under the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act of 1990, which is meant to make government salaries competitive with private sector pay, the president is allowed to preempt an automatic increase determined by the law’s formula by issuing an alternative pay plan by the end of August. Congress has the authority to override the proposed changes until December, when the White House can eventually choose to cement an alternate pay plan through an executive order.

In April 2025, the Office of Management and Budget initially instructed federal agencies to plan for a civilian federal pay freeze for the next calendar year. That August, Trump ultimately issued an alternative pay plan to Congress that authorized a 1% pay increase.

Trump last froze federal civilian workers’ salaries in December 2018 during a partial government shutdown, but reversed the decision in March 2019 to give a 1.9% raise on average to civilian employees. The last president to issue a multiyear freeze was Barack Obama, who imposed the change due to deficit concerns from 2011 to 2013.

entries.title: Trump Launches a New Military College for Space Force Recruits
entries.summary: The president said the academy, which also will serve as a pipeline for NASA, would be analogous to the U.S. Military Academy.
entries.content:
The United States Space Force will have its own Space Academy, with President Donald Trump announcing plans for the new military college on Friday at NASA’s Johnson Space Center.

“We’re going to have an academy for what the people in this room love the most,” Trump told the crowd in Houston.

Trump signed an executive order to begin creating the academy during a ceremony awarding the Artemis II flight crew with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor. The president was joined onstage by astronauts based at the center and the Artemis II crew, whom Trump called “very special people.”

“Great people, great men and women,” Trump said of the crew. “Incredible.”

Although details were scarce, Trump said the academy would be analogous to the United States Military Academy, which trains officers for the United States Army, or the Air Force Academy.

“It’s clear that we will need to educate and train an entire generation of skilled service members, engineers, and civil operators, and everything else to do what we have to do — and what we’re right now doing the best,” Trump said.

The academy would serve the United States Space Force, as well as NASA and the private spaceflight industry, according to the president.

The Space Force directed questions about the academy to the White House and NASA. Neither immediately responded to requests for comment.

The executive order established a “presidential commission on the United States Space Academy.” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will lead the commission. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, White House chief of staff Susie Wiles and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought will join him.

Within three months, the commission must submit details of the academy to Trump, including a framework of admissions and operations, whether to establish the academy within NASA and potential curriculum options.

Trump discussed constructing a new campus for the academy and added that he will choose the academy’s location “very shortly.”

An active Space Academy already exists on a NASA campus. The U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama — where Trump moved U.S. Space Command headquarters last year — hosts weeklong space camps for teenage space-lovers during the summer.

entries.title: Trump Pushes Major Meatpacking Change Just Days After Plea From Glenn Beck
entries.summary: The changes seemed to be inspired by the political commentator’s pleas to the president during a radio interview Wednesday.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump said Friday he is moving to change federal regulations as part of a bid to allow farmers and ranchers to process their own meat — a decision that came just days after conservative political commentator Glenn Beck made an impassioned plea to the president during a radio interview.

Trump said the changes would alleviate a “tremendous problem” posed by four large companies that control a vast majority of the nation’s meat processing plants. Ranchers and farmers are required to use facilities that comply with the U.S. Agriculture Department’s federal regulations and inspection requirements.

“They make life miserable for our wonderful Farmers and Ranchers, and I can’t let that happen, can I?” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “So, in order to break this powerful monopoly, with much of its ownership based outside of the U.S., I am authorizing legal documents to be drawn in order to allow Farmers and Ranchers to be given the right to PROCESS THEIR OWN FOOD. This should move quickly.”

The idea was first raised by Beck in a wide-ranging radio interview with Trump on Wednesday.

“Help us! Help us!” Beck told Trump, urging him to look into the “meat processing cartel.” Beck, who owns a ranch, argued there were people who “want to build processing plants everywhere,” but the stringent regulations governing slaughterhouses “are killing” cattle farmers across the country.

Trump’s move also comes after his administration faced swift backlash from farm organizations, ranchers associations and Republicans over the weekend for its decision to allow the tariff-free import of 300,000 metric tons of beef in an attempt to lower costs for consumers.

Current regulations require slaughterhouse facilities to abide by various labeling, sanitation and building requirements, as well as butchering standards laid out by the Humane Methods of Slaughter Act, according to the National Agricultural Law Center. Facilities must also allow continuous inspections by government personnel.

“So you’re saying with less regulation, you think the ranchers and farmers would do a very good job of processing the beef,” Trump asked Beck during their interview. The longtime conservative media stalwart replied, simply, “yes.”

“This is a very big thing you just told me,” Trump added later in the conversation. “You just gave me a very good idea.”

entries.title: Florida Democrat Hits Up a MAGA Lobbyist for Campaign Cash
entries.summary: David Jolly’s campaign solicited contributions from a GOP firm that employs his opponent’s former top aide.
entries.content:
Florida Democratic gubernatorial nominee David Jolly, a former Republican member of Congress, is going back to his roots and soliciting support from a GOP lobbyist.

On Thursday, a representative from Jolly’s campaign sent a personalized email to Sam Geduldig, a managing partner at the Republican lobbying firm CGCN, inviting Geduldig to a fundraiser and requesting a meeting.

“I am reaching out on behalf of David Jolly, the Democratic Nominee for Governor of Florida. We would love to schedule a meeting for you and David to discuss his campaign when he is in Washington, DC on September 16th,” the email reads, later adding, "if you are not able to join us for either event or would prefer some 1:1 time with David, let us know."

Geduldig, a staunch Republican and Trump supporter, is a prolific GOP donor, per Federal Election Commission records. Additionally, Harrison Fields, a partner at CGCN, previously served as senior adviser and communications director to Jolly’s Republican opponent, Rep. Byron Donalds.

A former lobbyist himself, Jolly has long made fighting corruption and special interests part of his political identity. He introduced an unsuccessful bill in 2016 that would ban members of Congress from directly soliciting campaign contributions, and he previously called for a ban on political donations from lobbyists.

“A former lobbyist asking lobbyists for money while complaining about lobbyist influence is next-level hypocrisy,” Geduldig said in a statement to NOTUS.

Mark Riddle, a senior adviser for the Jolly campaign, told NOTUS, “Neither our Florida nor our national finance leads knows this person,” referring to Geduldig.

“However, with Jolly now ahead, and Cook shifting the race in our favor, everyday Republicans in Tallahassee and D.C. have been lighting up our phones asking for meetings,” Riddle wrote. “Let the games begin.”

Jolly served as a Republican congressman for one term before attempting to run for Senate in 2016, but later reversed course and ran for reelection to his House seat. He lost to former Florida Gov. Charlie Crist, who also left the GOP and joined the Democratic Party during the Obama administration.

While Jolly tapped a longtime Florida lobbyist in June to lead his transition team, he has emphasized an anti-corruption message as a strategy to reach voters across the political spectrum.

“People feel the economic crisis, they’re exhausted by culture wars, they can smell corruption from Washington and Tallahassee,” Jolly told Politico this summer, “and so they’re performing in ways that don’t reflect voter registration.”

The Cook Political Report recently shifted the Florida gubernatorial election from “solidly Republican” to “likely Republican,” noting Jolly would still need a “significant financial boost” to compete with Donalds.

Lobbyists are a reliable source of campaign cash for members of Congress, and campaign contributions are an age-old way to open the door or build relationships with candidates and lawmakers. Even Geduldig has donated to a few Democrats over the years.

CGCN is one of the few all-Republican firms on K Street, and securing donations from the firm would also be a boon to the cross-party message the Jolly campaign is trying to cultivate. The Jolly campaign website says the gubernatorial race “isn’t about party,” and the email from Jolly’s team to Geduldig argues, “David can reach well beyond the traditional Democratic base.”

Other Republicans have proved willing to cross the aisle to back Democrats during the 2026 midterm election cycle, including a former staffer for Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas). After Cornyn lost his Senate primary, the staffer joined the Senate campaign for Democrat James Talarico, a move first reported by NOTUS.

entries.title: Republicans Buck Trump’s ‘Lake America’ Order: ‘Petty and Disappointing’
entries.summary: Republicans, including many from northern states whose jurisdictions share geographical ties with Canada, said the Great Lakes should be left alone.
entries.content:
Republican leaders in the Midwest and Northeast are signaling their unhappiness with President Donald Trump’s plans to rename Lake Ontario to “Lake America” as an apparent jab at Canada amid the two countries’ escalating trade war.

The pushback was particularly strong in northern states, including New York, the only state that borders the body of water.

Trump’s Thursday order requires Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to update the nomenclature used by the Geographic Names Information System, an agency that oversees federal maps and signage. But the order does not affect states or municipalities, whose leaders say it would require an exorbitant investment to change official government materials to reflect the change.

That included officials in Oswego, New York, a historic port city on the shores of Lake Ontario. The city’s Republican mayor, Robert Corradino, told a local TV station that the name change, if fully implemented, would be “a very costly endeavor.”

He added that Oswego had no current plans to update city-owned signage, pointing out that the town’s identity remains closely connected to Lake Ontario.

Vermont Gov. Phil Scott, a Republican and occasional critic of Trump’s, was more straightforward in his criticism.

“This is petty and disappointing,” he wrote Thursday on X. “We should be at the negotiating table, finding a path forward that strengthens both the U.S. and Canadian economies. Further escalating tensions does nothing to help American or Canadian families and businesses.”

Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany, whom Trump endorsed for Wisconsin governor, joked Thursday that the Great Lakes should retain their names, “unless you’re suggesting we name Lake Michigan, Lake Wisconsin.”

“Now I want to be clear, I said that all in jest,” Tiffany added, “The Great Lakes are Great Lakes, and we should leave them that way.”

The Republican candidate for New York governor, Bruce Blakeman, did not defend Trump’s move when asked by a reporter about it, instead resorting to humor.

“I was hoping to rename it Lake Blake!” he texted News10NBC.

Despite the pushback, some Republicans publicly supported Trump’s efforts — earning praise from the president.

Rep. Mike Lawler (R-New York) said in an interview with Fox Business Network that he didn’t think “people care about the name of the lake.”

“I do think they care about fair trade,” he added.

Trump later complimented Lawler’s “fantastic” broadcast appearance in a post on Truth Social.

Democrats, including New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, indicated Thursday that they would not abide by Trump’s order.

Some in Congress are also preparing to mount an opposition to the name change. Rep. Debbie Dingell (D-Michigan) told Politico she intends to file legislation Monday to block the name change. It’s unclear whether any Republicans will join her effort.

entries.title: Belgium Summons U.S. Ambassador Over a Social Media Post
entries.summary: This is the second time U.S. Ambassador Bill White has been reprimanded by Belgian authorities this year.
entries.content:
Belgian authorities plan to summon the U.S. ambassador for a reprimand this week after an incendiary social media post in which he mocked one of the country’s top officials, marking the second time this year that he has been called to answer for confrontational comments.

Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot told NOTUS he planned to make the request to U.S. Ambassador Bill White after he mocked Belgian Health Minister Frank Vandenbroucke. The spat came after Vandenbroucke proposed a law strengthening the warnings Belgium puts on alcohol advertisements.

“Who’s the biggest LOSER in Belgium?” White, who was appointed by Trump last year, displayed on Instagram’s story feature, posting what appeared to be an AI-generated picture of the health minister on a cigar box with text that read, “Damages every form of joy in life.”

Belgium has introduced robust new alcohol advertising standards, which require all alcohol advertisements to carry the warning “Alcohol is harmful to health” across a wide range of formats and media. The measures were spearheaded by Vandenbroucke and include a ban on alcohol advertising in media where at least 30% of the audience are minors.

Prévot said in a statement to NOTUS that the language used by White was “unacceptable” and that he planned to “summon him to my office in the following days.”

The U.S. ambassador was previously summoned by Belgian authorities in February for accusing the country of antisemitism and intervening in the country's judicial affairs.

At the time, Prévot had called White’s allegations “dangerous misinformation.”

entries.title: U.S. Military Uses New Laser Technology to Down ‘Cartel-Linked’ Drones
entries.summary: The operation was the first high-energy laser strike against cartel-linked drones, according to a statement from the U.S. Northern Command.
entries.content:
The U.S. military shot down three drones with a laser this week on the southern border, saying the autonomous aircraft were linked to cartels.

The operation, which took place Tuesday to Wednesday, was the first operation where the military used a high-energy laser against cartel-linked drones, according to a statement from the U.S. Northern Command. The military detected the “hostile” drones as part of activities posing a physical threat to U.S. soldiers and Customs and Border Protection personnel.

“Cartel networks are increasingly employing unmanned aircraft systems to facilitate illicit human-smuggling and actively spy on our personnel and law enforcement partners,” said Maj. Gen. Curtis Taylor, commander of the U.S. Northern Command’s southern border task force, in a statement. “By integrating layered countermeasures alongside advanced directed-energy capabilities like this laser system, we have made it clear that we will not tolerate hostile surveillance.”

The announcement did not specify where the drones were shot down or what cartels they belonged to.

CBP’s use of an anti-drone laser near Fort Bliss led to the sudden closure of airspace over the El Paso International Airport in February, according to The Associated Press. The closure, originally set to last for multiple days, led to a crisis among the government and aviation officials dealing with the shutdown for hours, NOTUS previously reported.
entries.author: Jackie Llanos

entries.title: National Park Service Green-Lights Trump’s Arch
entries.summary: The NPS will focus on pursuing measures to minimize the arch’s impact on the surrounding historic area, rather than choosing a new site altogether.
entries.content:
The National Park Service released a report Friday in support of President Donald Trump’s proposed arch, while acknowledging the adverse effects the new monument could have on the district’s most iconic memorials and landmarks.

The arch project is part of Trump’s push to reshape D.C. in his image by leaving a visible mark on the nation’s capital. Critics of the arch and Trump’s other beautification initiatives have argued that the renovations obstruct the district’s sightline — concerns validated throughout the agency’s report — while Democratic lawmakers say the president is bypassing necessary congressional approval to proceed with construction.

NPS’ review was mandated by the National Historic Preservation Act, which requires agencies to evaluate how proposed new construction could directly or adversely affect any nearby landmarks and provide solutions to minimize future harm.

The proposed 250-foot arch will be located at Memorial Circle, near Arlington National Cemetery, and the agency analyzed the surrounding 3.5-mile radius as part of its study. The 133-page report says its construction will likely disturb dozens of historic sites in the area, including the Arlington Memorial Bridge, the cemetery, the Lincoln Memorial and the National Mall.

The monument will adversely affect six out of 31 National Historic Landmarks in the proposed area, including the U.S. Capitol and the Pentagon — though the effects will mostly stem from altered sightlines and plans to light the area at night, rather than physical damage, the report noted.

While the panel acknowledged the “sensitive” nature of building an arch in the Memorial Circle landscape, the area’s significance makes it an “historically appropriate location” to build, the agency wrote.

The service repeatedly rejected moving the site or abandoning the project altogether.

“Alternative locations outside Memorial Circle are not reasonable avoidance alternatives,” the report said, saying the NPS will instead focus on measures to mitigate and minimize its impact within the limits of the selected location.

The U.S. Commission of Fine Arts approved the design in May, months after Trump overhauled the panel with his appointees.

The findings could play a role as the administration faces legal challenges over the arch. A group of veterans sued Trump in February over the structure’s potential sightline obstruction of Arlington National Cemetery — one of the sites Friday’s report says could be adversely affected.

The Park Service also compiled more than 100,000 public comments collected in June and July, many of which raised questions and concerns about the sightline obstruction, rushed timeline, cost, potential environmental impact and the project’s aesthetics.

“Some commenters asserted that the design resembles European triumphal arches, imperial, or authoritarian monuments and is not rooted in American traditions, diminishing the symbolism and integrity of the Lincoln Memorial and its surrounding landscape,” the agency wrote in an AI summary of comments submitted June 5-15.

entries.title: DHS Memo Sought to Deputize National Guard for Immigration Arrests
entries.summary: The document bypassed an 1878 law meant to restrict the president from using troops within U.S. borders, though none have arrested unauthorized immigrants.
entries.content:
A confidential Department of Homeland Security memo issued shortly after President Donald Trump returned to office gave officials a legal rationale for using National Guard troops as immigration officers, opening the door to a constitutional battle over the use of military personnel for domestic law-enforcement purposes.

The practice is limited by a once-obscure 1878 law called the Posse Comitatus Act, which is meant to restrict the president from using troops within U.S. borders. But in an effort to carry out Trump’s aggressive mass-deportation push, federal officials at multiple junctures ran into legal challenges while citing the law — including in Los Angeles, where Trump deployed National Guard troops against Gov. Gavin Newsom’s wishes and was later rebuked in court for running afoul of Posse Comitatus.

The April 2025 memo, obtained by American Oversight through a Freedom of Information Act request and shared with NOTUS, argues that National Guard members can be designated as federal immigration officers when they are ordered to serve outside their home states. The document authorized them to “perform immigration functions,” including arresting unauthorized immigrants — though no such instances have been reported.

The memo, penned by then-DHS general counsel Joseph Mazzara, argues that National Guard members can take on a different legal status when they are assigned to another state, effectively making them federal employees.

Politico first reported the memo.

Trump has repeatedly threatened to invoke the Insurrection Act, which would give him broader authority to deploy troops domestically. The law was originally written to provide the president greater options to respond to severe unrest — though critics argue the existence of undocumented immigrants does not qualify.

During Trump’s second term, the Supreme Court has limited his administration’s ability to deploy the National Guard for immigration enforcement, ruling in December that local forces would need to be incapacitated in some way before military personnel could be used for domestic purposes. The decision came after Illinois filed a legal challenge following a draconian immigration crackdown known as “Operation Midway Blitz” that employed National Guard troops.

National Guard troops have still assisted with background immigration work and provided security for federal agents carrying out immigration arrests, but the Trump administration has not yet openly directed the service members to directly carry out arrests.

Chioma Chukwu, the executive director of American Oversight, a nonprofit government watchdog group, said the memo should be alarming to Americans everywhere.

“Combined with the administration’s escalating claims about noncitizen voting, this theory could be used to put military forces near polling places under the guise of immigration enforcement,” Chukwu said in a statement. “The stakes extend well beyond immigration: This memo gives the president a ready-made workaround for using military power at home whenever the administration decides its agenda demands it.”

DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment from NOTUS, but told Politico that the letter would “speak for itself.”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has separately sought to use DHS to investigate alleged voter fraud. He and other administration officials have suggested that noncitizens are voting in large numbers and potentially swaying the results of U.S. elections — though they have provided little evidence to back up their claims.

“We will scrub all election records, looking for illegal aliens and those who are ineligible to vote, including those that somehow voted, yet they were deceased,” Mullin said in July.

entries.title: Vance and Zeldin Push for a Probe Into Biden’s Handling of East Palestine
entries.summary: The request comes after documents were made public showing federal officials’ concerns about contamination in the Ohio town following a train derailment in 2023.
entries.content:
Vice President JD Vance and Environmental Protection Agency head Lee Zeldin are calling for an independent investigation into the Biden administration’s response to the Norfolk Southern train derailment that released hazardous materials in East Palestine, Ohio, in 2023.

In a letter to the EPA’s Office of Inspector General, Vance and Zeldin say ongoing concerns about federal decisions that may have affected human health warrant review.

Documents released this week by a government watchdog group show federal officials had concerns about the number of deaths that could result from burning some of the hazardous chemicals inside the train. The documents also included an unpublished analysis of contamination concerns from one month after the derailment, which showed hazardous contaminants lingering in East Palestine.

After train rail cars carrying hazardous chemicals crashed in February 2023, worries about a massive explosion led Norfolk Southern to propose draining the chemical vinyl chloride out of five of those cars and setting it on fire. Nearby residents were evacuated before the plan went into effect.

The newly released documents show early EPA modeling projected that more than 1,900 people could die and thousands could get sick from the burning of that chemical. Later modeling reduced those numbers to 29 potential deaths and 163 injuries.

The National Transportation Safety Board later found that Norfolk Southern misrepresented the risk of the train cars exploding, and that the decision to vent and burn the chemicals was unnecessary.

East Palestine residents have remained concerned about their health since the disaster.

“The people of East Palestine deserve certainty about their health and the safety of their community. They did not get it from the Biden EPA,” Zeldin said in a statement.  “The Trump EPA is committed to correcting the mistakes of the past administration. We have done everything in our power since day one to protect human health and the environment in East Palestine, and that work will continue, guided by our commitment to gold-standard science.”

Earlier this year, the Trump administration opened an investigation into a subcontractor responsible for sampling groundwater at the train derailment site after it failed to meet data quality standards.
entries.author: Mara Hoplamazian
